title: Setup code
description: The JSON inside a setup code, basalt-setup.1.<b64url(deflate-raw(json))>.<check> (CONTRACT.md, Setup from your laptop). basalt init --remote makes it on the bot's machine; basalt init --setup-code reads it on the person's own computer. Never the agent's password (its SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier instead, which is sensitive) and never anything of the admin. Closed: an unknown key is refused. Rules a schema cannot state (guard.from <= guard.to, and < for UPGRADE; at least one table; a table in only one of write and read; the agent role <prefix>_agent_<name> at most 63 bytes; expiresAt no later than the setupId's UUIDv7 time plus 24 hours) are in CONTRACT.md. Golden fixtures: setup-code.fixtures.json.

install.description: INSTALL: the guard (migrations guard.from+1..guard.to), the agent role with its password set from the verifier, its grants, and a portal passkey when none is active.

agentChange.description: AGENT: an existing agent's tables, replaced by write and read as given; with a verifier its password is rotated, without one it is kept. Also applies missing migrations up to guard.to and registers a portal passkey when none is active.

upgrade.description: UPGRADE: the missing migrations up to guard.to only. No agent part: the password, grants and policies are unchanged.

format.description: Payload format. A decoder refuses any other value as a newer format (update basalt), not as a damaged code.

setupId.description: UUIDv7 made by basalt init --remote. Single use: recorded in basalt_meta.setups by the laptop's install transaction. Time-ordered, so a code older than the agent's latest recorded setup is refused.

target.description: The database the bot's engine connects to, from its password-less connection string. The laptop compares it with the admin connection string by database identity and refuses a mismatch (CO-17).

host.description: Host name or IP address, as in the bot's connection string.

supabaseRef.description: The Supabase project ref when the connection string names one: the pooler user postgres.<ref> or the direct host db.<ref>.supabase.co. Absent otherwise. With it, the project ref and database decide identity, so the pooler and the direct host of one project match.

guard.description: basalt_meta schema versions. from: the version the bot read with the agent credential, 0 when it could not read one. to: the version the bot's build installs.

build.description: The bot's basalt version, named when the laptop's binary is older than guard.to (update basalt on this computer to at least <build>).

table.description: schema.table of plain (unquoted, lowercase) identifiers; never a system schema or basalt_meta.

verifier.description: The agent password's SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier (RFC 5802, RFC 7677), as Postgres stores it: SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:<salt>$<StoredKey>:<ServerKey>, standard base64, a 16-byte random salt and 4096 iterations. Sensitive: it is not the password, but with one observed SCRAM exchange of the role it lets its holder log in as the agent (CONTRACT.md, The setup code).

agentName.description: The agent's name (guard.Names); its role <prefix>_agent_<name> fits in 63 bytes.

expiresAt.description: RFC 3339 UTC, whole seconds: 24 hours after basalt init --remote made the code (CO-13).
